content.text:
I rebased `feat/skills` onto `main` (which now has #61, AGENTS.md) and force-pushed it as one commit, `23fa248`. `npm run check` passes, and commitlint now passes too.

**commitlint:** the only error was `body-max-line-length`, because the commit body was one long line. I rewrapped it to under 100 characters and added a line saying where the skills section sits relative to #61's section. The subject is unchanged.

**Merge conflicts:** #61 added its own built-in extension, `pi-action-context`, with the `project_context` section. I kept both extensions separate rather than merging them into one. They install in this order: `coding-tools`, `pi-action-context`, `pi-action` (`available_skills`), then the user's extensions. So user extensions can still wrap both sections.
- **`src/run.ts`:** setup returns both `context` and `skills`. `Thread.open` gets `projectContext: context` and `extensions: [createBuiltinExtension({ skills }), ...extensions]`.
- **`src/durable-extensions.ts`:** user extensions can't take the names `coding-tools`, `pi-action-context` or `pi-action`.
- **`CONTRIBUTING.md` and `docs/security.md`:** I kept both sides: the context-files rows and section, and the skills ones.
- **`docs/extensions.md`:** the install order and the list of reserved names now include both built-in extensions.

**Doc changes beyond the conflicts:**
- **`docs/prompts.md`:** the system prompt list now has `available_skills` as item 2. The line saying the prompt can be empty now mentions skills.
- **`docs/extensions.md`:** the "unique name" line also lists `pi-action-context` as a reserved name.

There is a test that a user extension can't use the name `pi-action-context`. I didn't add the same test for `pi-action`.

The PR description still says "#53 can add the AGENTS.md section to it", but #61 put that section in its own extension instead. You may want to edit that line.
